&reftitle.description;
boolshmop_delete Shmopshmop
shmop_delete marks a shared memory block for deletion.
The data is not destroyed at once: the segment is destroyed when the last process detaches from it, that is, in PHP, when the last Shmop object for it is freed. Until then, the given object and every process attached earlier keep reading and writing it. The key is released immediately, so a later call to shmop_open with the same key creates a new segment, independent of the old one.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns &true; on success, or &false; on failure. If the removal is refused, for example because the segment belongs to another user, an E_WARNING is emitted and &false; is returned. Calling the function again on the same object returns &true;.

&reftitle.examples;
Deleting shared memory block
<?php shmop_delete($shm_id); ?>
This example will mark the shared memory block identified by $shm_id for deletion.
